group_assessment.counts_measured: Not measured as a count. 🔴 MEASURED AS SOMETHING MORE USEFUL: THIS PAPER SPANS THE TWO LITERATURES YESTERDAY'S REVIEW SHOWED TO BE DISJOINT. Farooq's biophysics laboratory at Miami with Nawaz; Aqeilan and Salah and Bar-Mag from the Hebrew University; and Marius Sudol, who defined the WW domain class. The Chang axis is absent and the Aqeilan axis is a co-author. A quantitative bridge built by the people whose primary literature this corpus already rests on.
group_assessment.weighting: 🔴 THE OBSERVATION IS THE STRONGEST KIND THIS CORPUS HAS AND THE INTERPRETATION IS THE MOST RESTRAINED, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF EVERY PAPER READ IN THE LAST TWO DAYS. The observations are isothermal titration calorimetry with errors from at least three independent measurements, alanine scans, circular dichroism, differential scanning calorimetry, molecular dynamics and a cell-based pulldown — dissociation constants with standard deviations, stoichiometries fitted rather than assumed. They do not depend on how anyone reads a blot. The interpretation is correspondingly narrow: the authors say 'we are tempted to suggest' where they speculate, mark NBD rather than reporting a weak number, and their central negative — WW2 binds nothing — is supported by ITC, CD, DSC, structural modelling AND a pulldown. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR WEIGHTING IS UNUSUAL AND WORTH STATING PLAINLY: this is the one paper in the corpus where a number can settle an argument that blots have been carrying, and it settles one recorded here yesterday.

entries.proposition: 🔴 WWOX HAS ONE FUNCTIONAL PPXY-BINDING DOMAIN, NOT TWO, AND THIS IS MEASURED RATHER THAN INFERRED. The isolated WW2 domain shows no detectable interaction with ANY of the five PPXY motifs tested across WBP1 and WBP2. The result is not a single assay: it is ITC, a GST pulldown in HEK293 cells, circular dichroism, differential scanning calorimetry and structural modelling agreeing, and the structural reason is given — R25 and W44 in WW1 are replaced by E66 and Y85 in WW2, and restoring them by an E66R/Y85W double substitution restores binding.
entries.snippet: the WW2 domain does not appear to interact with any PPXY motifs within either WBP1 or WBP2 within the sensitivity of our measurements
entries.anchor: Results and Discussion, 'WW1 domain but not WW2 domain of WWOX binds to PPXY motifs within WBP1 and WBP2', describing Figure 3 and Table 1
entries.found_or_sought: sought — the paper was opened to find out how many binding sites WWOX has, because an inference recorded here yesterday assumed two

entries.proposition: AND THE AFFINITIES ARE WEAK, WHICH THE PAPER'S OWN PHRASE 'PHYSIOLOGICALLY-RELEVANT MICROMOLAR RANGE' DOES NOT CONVEY. Table 1, isolated WW1 domain: WBP2_PY3 at 122 ± 1 μM, WBP1_PY2 at 366 ± 23 μM, and NO BINDING DETECTED for the other three motifs. Binding is enthalpy-driven with unfavourable entropy in both cases. INFERENZA: an interaction at 122 μM is not a stable complex at physiological concentrations — it is a transient, high-turnover contact, and any model in which WWOX HOLDS a partner in the cytoplasm has to account for how a 122 μM interaction holds anything.

entries.proposition: 🔴 AND THE TANDEM BINDS ONE PEPTIDE, NOT TWO — WHICH CORRECTS AN INFERENCE THIS CORPUS RECORDED YESTERDAY. Table 5 gives the wild-type WW1-WW2 tandem binding WBP2_PY3 with a fitted stoichiometry n = 1.05 ± 0.01 at Kd 49 ± 1 μM, and WBP1_PY2 at n = 0.99 ± 0.04. ONE LIGAND PER TANDEM. Only the ENGINEERED WW1-WW2rw tandem, with WW2's binding restored, reaches n = 2.00. YESTERDAY, ADJUDICATING PMID 16061658, I RECORDED THE AUTHORS' HYPOTHESIS THAT WWOX OUT-BINDS YAP 'due to the interaction of WWOX with BOTH the PPxY motifs of ErbB-4' AND CARRIED IT FORWARD AS 'TWO CONTACTS AGAINST ONE — THE COMPETITION IS ASYMMETRIC'. That mechanism is now measured and it is not two contacts: wild-type WWOX presents ONE functional site and binds ONE PPXY peptide. Aqeilan's own word was 'perhaps' and the hedge was recorded with it; what is corrected is my restatement, not their claim. WHAT SURVIVES IS AN AFFINITY ADVANTAGE, NOT A VALENCY ADVANTAGE — see entries[3].

entries.proposition: WHAT THE TANDEM ACTUALLY BUYS, AND IT IS REAL: BETTER THAN TWO-FOLD AFFINITY AND A WIDER CAPTURE RADIUS. WW1 alone binds WBP2_PY3 at 122 μM; the tandem binds it at 49 μM. And the tandem acquires binding to WBP2_PY2, which WW1 alone does not detectably bind. So the second WW domain matters — not by adding a site but by making the first one better and broader. That is a mechanistically different claim from the one this corpus was carrying, and it is the one the data support.
entries.snippet: the WW2 domain not only plays a role in augmenting ligand binding affinity of WW1 domain but also increases its capture radius
entries.anchor: Results and Discussion, 'WW2 domain chaperones WW1 domain in the context of WW1-WW2 tandem domains'
entries.found_or_sought: found — read in sequence, and it is what replaces the valency story

entries.proposition: AND THE STRUCTURAL SURPRISE THAT EXPLAINS IT: THE BINDING DOMAIN IS THE DISORDERED ONE. WW1, which binds, is largely unstructured and folds upon ligand binding; WW2, which binds nothing, is a well-folded β-sheet with a melting temperature about 7°C higher. The authors state the general lesson themselves — lack of structure does not equate to lack of binding, nor the reverse. INFERENZA WITH A BEARING ON THE REFERENCE GENOTYPE: a missense variant in WW1 is a variant in an intrinsically disordered segment that folds only on engagement, so predicting its effect from a static structure is predicting the wrong state — which is exactly the caution PMID 30356099 raised from the clinical side when it noted that every missense call in the largest WOREE cohort rests on in silico prediction.
entries.snippet: it is the WW1 domain not the WW2 domain that is structurally disordered
entries.anchor: Results and Discussion, 'WW1 domain but not WW2 domain of WWOX appears to be structurally disordered', describing Figure 5
entries.found_or_sought: sought — asked why the non-binding domain is the conserved one, and the answer inverts the expectation

entries.proposition: THE ROLE THE PAPER ASSIGNS WW2, STATED AS A HYPOTHESIS AND SUPPORTED BY FOUR INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENTS. An orphan domain with no physiological ligand, evolved as a chaperone that imparts structural and thermal stability on WW1. Recorded because it is the sentence a downstream reader will quote, and because it makes the tandem architecture meaningful without making it bivalent.
entries.snippet: the WW2 domain of WWOX is likely an orphan WW domain without any physiological ligands and that it may have evolved as a chaperone

entries.proposition: 🔴 AND THE FINDING THIS CORPUS DID NOT KNOW IT NEEDED: A SEQUENCE-LEVEL BASIS FOR THE WWOX-ITCH COMPETITION, FROM 2012. Searching the human proteome for WW domains carrying an arginine and a tryptophan at the positions that make WW1 a binder, the authors find only a handful — AND EVERY ONE OF THEM BELONGS TO THE E3 UBIQUITIN LIGASE FAMILY, NAMING ITCH AND NEDD4. So WWOX's binding domain shares its recognition signature specifically with the ligases whose substrates it is later shown to contest. THE ARC THIS CORPUS HOLDS IS 'WWOX COMPETES WITH ITCH ON ΔNp63α' FROM PMID 23370280 (2013), READ AS AN OBSERVATION. This paper predates it and supplies a structural reason the observation should have been expected. It does not make ITCH selectivity a DATO — nothing here manipulates ITCH — but it moves the competition from coincidence to prediction.
entries.snippet: all of these WW domains belong to the E3 ubiquitin ligase family of enzymes, such as ITCH and NEDD4
entries.anchor: Results and Discussion, 'Wildtype WW1 domain and the engineered WW2_RW domain appear to share high sequence similarity with ubiquitin ligase family of WW domains', describing Figure 9
entries.found_or_sought: sought — went looking for what else shares WW1's binding chemistry, and the answer named the E3 ligase this corpus has been arguing about for two days

entries.proposition: AND THE AUTHORS DRAW THE CONSEQUENCE THEMSELVES, HEDGED AND WORTH QUOTING HEDGED. That WWOX's WW1 may compete with the cellular partners of ubiquitin ligases and thereby neutralise their function — offered as 'we are tempted to suggest', not as a result. IPOTESI, and the corpus should carry the modal: it is a proposal built on a sequence alignment, not a measurement of competition.
entries.snippet: the WW1 domain of WWOX may compete with cellular partners of ubiquitin ligases and, in so doing, modulate or neutralize their physiological function

entries.proposition: THE RECOGNITION MOTIF IS LONGER THAN PPXY, WHICH CHANGES WHAT COUNTS AS A WWOX BINDING SITE. Alanine scanning across the WBP2_PY3 peptide shows that proline at −2 and tyrosine at +4 are required for high affinity, making PXPPXYY the optimal consensus rather than the minimal PPXY. INFERENZA WITH PRACTICAL FORCE: any inventory of 'WWOX partners' assembled by scanning proteomes for PPXY overstates the set, because most PPXY motifs lack the extended determinants — and this paper shows three of five motifs in two genuine adaptor proteins are not bound at all.

entries.proposition: AND THE AUTHORS FRAME THE WWOX-YAP COMPETITION AS AN OPEN QUESTION IN 2012, SEVEN YEARS AFTER THE PAPER THIS CORPUS ADJUDICATED. Aqeilan is a co-author here. The sentence says the ABILITY OR LACK THEREOF of WWOX to compete with YAP may be a defining event — a conditional, from the same laboratory that reported the competition in PMID 16061658. Recorded because it is the strongest available evidence that the hedge in that 2005 conclusion — 'WWOX and YAP MAY compete' — was meant, and was still meant seven years later.
